tagline: Up the Provo River, past a waterfall that falls twice.
intro: From Orem the byway takes US 189 up Provo Canyon beside the Provo River, between Mount Timpanogos and Mount Cascade, under gnarled walls and jagged rock grown thick with forest. At the top of the canyon it passes Deer Creek Reservoir, then leaves the highway for SR-113, through Midway and on into Heber City.

The canyon was the settlers' way over the Wasatch. A road was put through it in 1858, and permanent settlement in the Heber Valley followed in 1858 and 1859. The railroad came up the canyon in 1899, and part of its line still carries excursion trains between Heber City and Vivian Park.

moments.title: Bridal Veil Falls
moments.text: A double cataract 607 feet tall, in sight of the road, that once had a six-passenger tram to a lodge on the cliff top until an avalanche in 1996 wrecked the machinery.

moments.title: Deer Creek Reservoir
moments.text: An earthfill dam finished in 1941 holds back the Provo River at the top of the canyon, storing water for the Salt Lake and Utah valleys.

moments.title: Midway
moments.text: Two early settlements on Snake Creek merged in the 1860s around Fort Midway, built halfway between them, and the fort's site is now the town square.
